blocks.text: Paulus, in his Clavis in Psalmos, p. 282, thinks that the word עכשוב, a ἅπαξ λεγομενον [hapax legomenon], owes its origin to a faulty division of words: instead of what we now have, חמת עכשוב תחת שפתימו, we should read חמת עכשו בתחת שפתימו, they gather wrath (compare Arabic عكش [ʿakasha], to gather) under their lips. This conjecture seems to me to be rejected chiefly for this reason: in the first part of the verse there had preceded שננו לשונם כמו נחש, they sharpen their teeth like serpents, so that the parallelism of members requires in the other part of the verse another name of a serpent; and that this is עכשוב itself Bochart, I think, sufficiently shows in this chapter.
